questions.question: 419. A trader mixes 26 kg of rice at Tk 20 per kg with 30 kg of rice of other variety at Tk. 36 per kg and sells the mixture at Tk. 30 per kg. His profit percent is:
questions.explain:
Question: A trader mixes 26 kg of rice at Tk 20 per kg with 30 kg of rice of other variety at Tk. 36 per kg and sells the mixture at Tk. 30 per kg. His profit percent is:

Solution: 
C.P. of 56 kg rice = (26 × 20 + 30 × 36)
= (520 + 1080)
=1600 taka

S.P. of 56 kg rice = (56 × 30)
= 1680 taka

∴ Profit = 1680 - 1600
= 80 taka

 ∴ Profit percentage = (80/1600) × 100% = 5%

questions.question: 418. A train can travel 50% faster than a car. Both start from point A at the same time and reach point B 75 kms away from A at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 12.5 minutes while stopping at the stations. The speed of the car is:
questions.explain:
Question: A train can travel 50% faster than a car. Both start from point A at the same time and reach point B 75 kms away from A at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 12.5 minutes while stopping at the stations. The speed of the car is:

Solution: 
Let speed of the car be x kmph.
Then, speed of the train = 150x/100 = 3x/2

Now
(75/x) - {75/(3x/2)} = 125/(10 × 60)
(75/x) - (50/x) = 5/24
(75 - 50)/x = 5/24
25/x = 5/24
5x = 24 × 25
x = ( 24 × 25)/5
x = 120 kmph

questions.question: 417. 4 mat-weavers can weave 4 mats in 4 days. At the same rate, how many mats would be woven by 8 mat-weavers in 8 days?
questions.explain:
Question: 4 mat-weavers can weave 4 mats in 4 days. At the same rate, how many mats would be woven by 8 mat-weavers in 8 days?

Solution:
4 mat-weavers in 4 days weave = 4 mats
∴ 1 mat-weavers in 1 days weave = 4/(4 × 4) mats
∴ 8 mat-weavers in 8 days weave = (4 × 8 × 8)/(4 × 4) mats
= 16 mats

questions.question: 416. One fourth of the students of a school play cricket and two-third of the rest play football. The remaining 400 students do not play either of the games. How many students are there in the school?
questions.explain:
Question: One fourth of the students of a school play cricket and two-third of the rest play football. The remaining 400 students do not play either of the games. How many students are there in the school?

Solution:
Total number of students in a school be N. 

Total number of students who play Cricket = N/4

Rest are = N - N/4
= 3N/4

Total number of students who play Football = 3N/4 × 2/3
= 6N/12
= N/2

Total number of students who play Cricket or Football = N/4  + N/2
= 3N/4

Total number of students who do not play any Game = N - 3N/4
= N/4

ATQ,
N/4 = 400
⇒ N = 400 × 4
⇒ N = 1600

questions.question: 415. A pupil's marks were wrongly entered as 83 instead of 63. Due to that the average marks for the class got increased by half (1/2). The number of pupils in the class is:
questions.explain:
Question: A pupil's marks were wrongly entered as 83 instead of 63. Due to that the average marks for the class got increased by half (1/2). The number of pupils in the class is:

Solution:
Let there be x pupils in the class.
Total increase in marks = x × (1/2) = x/2

Here,
x/2 = (83 - 63)
⇒ x/2 = 20 
⇒ x = 40

questions.question: 414. Sachin is younger than Rahul by 7 years. If their ages are in the respective ratio of 7 : 9, how old is Sachin?
questions.explain:
Question: Sachin is younger than Rahul by 7 years. If their ages are in the respective ratio of 7 : 9, how old is Sachin?

Solution:
Let
Rahul 's age be x years.
Sachin's age = (x - 7) years.

Now
(x - 7)/x = 7/9
9x - 63 = 7x
9x - 7x = 63
2x = 63
x = 31.5 

Sachin's age = (x - 7) years.
= (31.5 - 7) years.
= 24.5 years.
